note: Sourced facts for fact cards. Each 'fit' lists what must be visible in a clip for the fact to be about it.

facts.fact: When Miles wears the Into the Spider-Verse suit, he moves at a lower framerate than the rest of the game, a nod to the film's animation. It is a suit mod that can be turned off at any time.
facts.quote: Kotaku: "Miles actually moves at a lower framerate when wearing the suit than in the rest of the game, a great nod to a similar animation technique used in Into the Spider-Verse"

facts.fact: In the Into the Spider-Verse suit, some of Miles' attacks are accompanied by comic book style POW! and THWACK! icons.
facts.quote: Push Square: "When Miles goes into combat, some of his attacks are accompanied by comic book style POW! and THWACK! icons."

facts.fact: The Vibe the Verse suit mod lets Miles leap into the Spider-Verse and makes his suit mimic the look of a different Earth.
facts.quote: GamesRadar+: "Vibe the Verse: Use this mod to leap into the Spider-Verse and cause the attached suit to mimic the aesthetic of a different Earth."

facts.fact: A bodega's resident cat, also named Spider-Man, is nabbed in a robbery. Miles rescues him from a warehouse, tucked inside a backpack, and can earn a suit with the cat riding in that backpack.
facts.quote: GamesRadar+: "this one had an adorable resident cat (also named Spider-Man) who was sadly nabbed in the robbery, as well."

facts.fact: The Spider-Cat is not just cosmetic: when Miles performs finishing moves, the cat leaps out of the backpack and slashes foes.
facts.quote: Kotaku: "when you perform finishing moves, the cat will leap out of the backpack and slash foes"

facts.fact: Miles got completely new swinging animations, and Game Informer's Andrew Reiner said his movements are inspired by skydiving acrobatics.
facts.quote: GamesRadar+: "Yes. Completely new. Miles' movements are inspired by skydiving acrobatics."

facts.fact: Miles can bust out more than 20 distinct air tricks while swinging, like a Tony Hawk character, and each trick grants a little experience.
facts.quote: Kotaku: "Like a Tony Hawk character, he can bust out more than 20 distinct tricks."

facts.fact: A burst of Venom can send Miles higher into the air or into a quick dash while exploring.
facts.quote: Game Informer: "A burst of Venom sends him higher into the air or into a quick dash, and both add a bit more superhero might to exploration."

facts.fact: The Venom Jump move propels Miles 15 feet into the air, while Venom Punch is a devastating charge attack.
facts.pairs_with: venom, combat, venom jump, venom punch
facts.flag: Single source (VGC, from Game Informer's preview).
facts.quote: VGC: "One move, Venom Jump, propels Miles 15 feet into the air, while Venom Punch is described as a devastating charge attack."

facts.fact: Miles' Venom attacks, triggered by holding L1 and pressing face buttons, need a Venom Meter that works like Peter's Focus Meter.
facts.quote: VGC: "Players must fill up a Venom Meter (which is like Peter’s Focus Meter) in order to use them"

facts.fact: Miles' new Venom abilities put a greater emphasis on area-of-effect attacks, since he often faces a crowd of enemies.
facts.quote: GamesRadar+: "The director says that the introduction of the new venom abilities really changes up combat, putting a greater emphasis on area-of-effect attacks."

facts.fact: Miles can turn invisible with camouflage, and enemies who lose sight of him return to their patterns, so you can try picking them off silently again.
facts.quote: Game Informer: "Enemies can lose sight of Miles and return to their patterns, so you can try picking them off silently again."

facts.fact: Miles' camouflage also makes snipers lose track of him, and it can be used in the middle of an all-out brawl.
facts.quote: Kotaku: "The camouflage will also cause snipers to lose track of you, making it arguably the most helpful trick in Miles’ book."

facts.fact: Miles earns a one-hit-kill finisher move every 15 hits in a combo.
facts.quote: Kotaku: "You earn a one-hit-kill finisher move every 15 hits."

facts.fact: Enemies Miles webs up in stealth takedowns dangle in plain sight, yet no one else notices them.
facts.quote: Kotaku: "Even though webbed enemies will dangle in plain sight, no one else will notice them"

facts.fact: A suit mod shows whether enemies will notice your stealth takedowns, with lines connecting the characters.
facts.quote: Push Square: "One shown is a mod that tells you if enemies will notice your stealth takedowns, indicated by lines connecting the characters."

facts.fact: Swiping left on the touchpad brings up a phone with the Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man app, which replaces the first game's police scanner for finding crimes and activities.
facts.pairs_with: app, phone, crimes, side activities, hud
facts.quote: VGC: "Swiping left on the DualSense’s touchpad brings up a phone, where players can find the new Friendly Neighbourhood Spider App."

facts.fact: Miles Morales' Photo Mode lets players move and place up to three lights to set up their shots.
facts.quote: VGC: "Players can move and place up to three lights to create ideal settings for their shots"

facts.fact: The game's first boss fight sees Miles face Rhino after he escapes from a cargo container moving through Harlem, a set piece Game Informer called far larger in scope than anything in the first game.
facts.quote: VGC: "The mag describes the set piece as “far larger in scope than anything seen in the first game”."

facts.fact: Early in the game Miles climbs onto Rhino's back and runs through a shopping mall, and a trophy asks you to smash into 15 breakable objects while steering him.
facts.quote: Push Square: "you'll climb onto the back of Rhino and run through a shopping mall."

facts.fact: A statue of Stan Lee stands in the Upper West Side, not far from Central Park, and interacting with it unlocks the Best Fries In Town trophy.
facts.pairs_with: stan lee, statue, tribute, trophy, easter eggs
facts.quote: TheGamer: "Finding and interacting with the statue, which can be found in the Upper West Side not far from Central Park, will even unlock the Best Fries In Town trophy."

facts.fact: The Wakandan embassy from the first game now stands on Boseman Way, a tribute to Black Panther actor Chadwick Boseman.
facts.quote: TheGamer: "the Wakandan embassy, which was also part of Marvel's Spider-Man can now be found on Boseman Way."

facts.fact: Two references in the game reveal X-Men's Dazzler to be a pretty big pop star in Insomniac's Spider-Man universe.
facts.quote: TheGamer: "There are two references to X-Men's Dazzler in the game, revealing the mutant to be a pretty big pop star in Insomniac's Spider-Verse."

facts.fact: Swim far out to sea and you can find boats of unfinished-looking NPCs, as in the 2018 game. In Miles Morales one of them wears a post-it note asking players if they missed them.
facts.pairs_with: easter eggs, boats, npcs, ocean, map edge
facts.quote: Screen Rant: "What's even funnier is that one of them wears a post-it note asking players if they missed them, a subtle nod to their inclusion in the first installment."

facts.fact: Spider-Training challenges start from a computer Peter Parker left behind and come in three types: Combat, Traversal and Stealth. Each one beaten grants a skill you cannot earn any other way.
facts.quote: Push Square: "interact with the computer left behind by Peter Parker to begin the activity."

facts.fact: After Peter's training challenges, a secret last test pits Miles against a virtual Vulture.
facts.quote: Screen Rant: "The last quest is known as The Final Test and brings in a virtual Vulture to combat against."

facts.fact: Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales has 69 collectibles to find, including 16 Time Capsules, 8 Postcards and 35 Underground Caches.
facts.quote: Push Square: "Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales has 69 collectibles for you to find."

facts.fact: When you track an Underground cache, the distance compass works in three dimensions, so 83m means 83 meters away in any direction.
facts.quote: Kotaku: "be wary that the resulting compass operates on a three-dimensional plane, rather than a two-dimensional one."

facts.fact: Miles' dad and Uncle Aaron used to record the sounds of the city together, hoping to build a song they never finished. The Sound Sample collectibles let Miles gather the recordings to polish it off.
facts.flag: Sources differ on the count (9 or 10 samples); do not state a number.
facts.quote: GamesRadar+: "The pair would record the sounds of the city together, hoping to eventually build a song out of it, which they never finished."

facts.fact: In C.J. Walker Park there is a DJ spinning songs, and Miles can wander over and dance in front of him.
facts.quote: GamesRadar+: "You can even wander over to the DJ to dance in front of him, even if Miles' moves aren't quite there yet."

facts.fact: On PS5, the game has ray-traced reflections under ice and snow and on wet streets, including holiday lighting reflecting off them.
facts.flag: PS5 version only. Single source (Game Informer).
facts.quote: Game Informer: "We have ray-traced reflections under ice and snow and wet streets at different times of day"

facts.fact: On PS5, dying or fast travelling brings near-instant loads with no loading screens, while the PS4 version keeps the loading screens and subway transitions.
facts.quote: Game Informer: "If you die or if you fast travel there are near-instant loads."

facts.fact: The game is set in wintertime, about a year after the first game, with Marvel's New York covered in snow just before Christmas break.
facts.quote: PlayStation Blog: "It’s now wintertime, about a year after the events of the first game. Marvel’s New York is covered in snow"

facts.fact: Insomniac compared the game's overall scope to Uncharted: The Lost Legacy, and Game Informer found it runs at roughly half the length of the 2018 game.
facts.quote: PlayStation Blog: "one that’s more akin to a game like Uncharted: The Lost Legacy in terms of overall scope."

facts.fact: Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales sold through 4.1 million units across PS5 and PS4 by the end of December 2020, in under two months on sale.
facts.quote: Push Square: "has sold through 4.1 million units as of the end of December."

facts.fact: There are 19 suits to unlock in Miles Morales. You can collect 18 in a single playthrough, but the final one needs New Game+.
facts.quote: Push Square: "There are 19 suits to unlock in Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales."

facts.fact: Miles can use Remote Mines on electrical panels to quickly clear out multiple enemies.
facts.quote: Push Square: "You can use Remote Mines on electrical panels to quickly and easy clear out multiple enemies."

facts.fact: Accessibility options include narrated American Sign Language lines and numerous ways to tweak subtitles for readability.
facts.quote: GameSpot: "There’s a narrated ASL option, and numerous ways to tweak your subtitles for improved readability."

facts.fact: The Contrast Options accessibility setting can show the hero, allies and enemies in solid single colors to help with visibility.
facts.quote: GameSpot: "Including solid single colors on the hero, allies, enemies, etc."

facts.fact: A mural in the city develops through the game as NPCs slowly add to it, and it ends up celebrating Miles as a hero.
facts.quote: Screen Rant: "Some players never discover this piece of art, which NPCs are slowly adding to."
